description: The relational operator <> (ISO §2023:8.7.5.2 SR11: "<> is an abbreviation for NOT EQUAL"; a special character word of §2023:8.3.2.4.2 SR2). A COBOL-2014 INTRODUCTION. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965; PB3602, PB3604): COBOL-85's relational operators are the GREATER / LESS / EQUAL forms with their symbols and NOT, 'IS NOT GREATER THAN is equivalent to IS LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO' (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1), with no <>; the 2002 text has none either, its clause 8.7.5.2 ending its abbreviation rules at '<= is an abbreviation for LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO.' (§2002:8.7.5.2 SR8) and its special character words passing from 'Relational operator - less than or equal' straight to the comment indicator (§2002:8.3.1.1.3.1); 2014 adds '<> is an abbreviation for NOT EQUAL.' (§2014:8.7.5.2 SR11) and the word 'Relational operator - not equal' (§2014:8.3.1.1.3.1), and §2014:E.3 item 23 states the change: 'Relational operator enhancement. The symbol' <> 'has been added as an extended relational operator. It is an abbreviation for "not equal".' §2023:8.7.5.2 SR11 and §2023:8.3.2.4.2 SR2 carry both. The word forms NOT EQUAL TO and NOT = are COBOL-85 and stay legal at every edition. Its siblings of §2023:8.3.2.4.2 are different rows: & (concat-operator-2002), >> (the directive rows), :: (inline-method-invocation-2002) and *> (floating-comment-indicator-2002). Gated in ONE place, the VersionConformancePass parse arm on comparisonOperator (kb/Work PB1459): the NOTEQUAL token appears in no other rule.
vcr: VCR row 7.26 - the 2002->2014 extended relational operator (§2014:E.3 item 23); special character words (§2023:8.3.2.4.2)
